The [spec](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/vkGetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceFormatsKHR.html) states:

> If pSurfaceFormats is NULL, then the number of format pairs supported for the given surface is returned in pSurfaceFormatCount. Otherwise, pSurfaceFormatCount must point to a variable set by the application to the number of elements in the pSurfaceFormats array, and on return the variable is overwritten with the number of structures actually written to pSurfaceFormats. If the value of pSurfaceFormatCount is less than the number of format pairs supported, at most pSurfaceFormatCount structures will be written, and [VK_INCOMPLETE](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html) will be returned instead of [VK_SUCCESS](https://docs.vulkan.org/refpages/latest/refpages/source/VkResult.html), to indicate that not all the available format pairs were returned.

This seems to indicate that we should accept both `VK_SUCCESS` and `VK_INCOMPLETE`, but still return an error if any other status is returned.

I'm concerned this condition as written might hide legitimate errors, while still reporting `VK_INCOMPLETE` as an error, unless I'm reading the logic wrong here.

Alternatively, would there be any value in re-querying the surface format count if we get `VK_INCOMPLETE` until we actually get all of the surface formats?

> I'm concerned this condition as written might hide legitimate errors, while still reporting VK_INCOMPLETE as an error, unless I'm reading the logic wrong here.

You're correct in that assumption, actually. I'm assuming that it'll only write a lower number whenever it returns `VK_INCOMPLETE`, but I suppose that it could keep the number the same if any other error would return. The initial idea here was that `VK_INCOMPLETE` is only an error if there's less formats than we expected, but that also isn't as serious so long as there's a non-zero number of formats.

> Alternatively, would there be any value in re-querying the surface format count if we get VK_INCOMPLETE until we actually get all of the surface formats?

I didn't want to add much more code here given I'm not that experienced with Vulkan, but it's certainly worth a try. I'll update the code to do that instead.
This doesn't look right, it will error regardless of any success in the loop above
Yeah, that's definitely not right. Will fix it now (sorry about CI!)
Can you add another `formats.resize(format_count)` after here, to be on the safe side? The Vulkan spec says format_count is updated with the actual amount of surface formats.
This second resize seems redundant now that we resize in the loop.
Same here, should be redundant now.
It's not redundant, see [my previous review](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/119344#discussion_r3232610780). GetPhysicalDeviceSurfaceFormatsKHR can update format_count and make it smaller.
ah, ok, didn't realize that could happen. Thanks!
